title: Five unsolved problems worth building a career on
description: The agentic era is creating some of the hardest problems in software, and extraordinary career opportunities for the people who solve them.
h1: Five unsolved problems worth building a career on
toc: Five problems worth building a career on
1. Engineering | Permissions and the write path
2. Design | Distinction, now with a mystery user
excerpt: The agentic era is creating some of the hardest problems in software, and extraordinary career opportunities for the people who solve them.

segments.t: I’ve led Talent at Attio as we’ve grown into a team of 200+. The best part of my job is meeting candidates excited about our hardest problems and employees solving them. As agents do more of the work,
systems of record become more valuable
. That transition is creating some of the hardest problems in software, and extraordinary career opportunities for the people who solve them.

I spend my days sharing our biggest challenges with exceptional people across Europe, the US and now APAC. But things are moving so quickly that I wanted to share five of the most interesting problems we're working on at Attio, and why they're worth building a career on.
For context, there's an argument that the system of record is the old idea: a productivity tool people logged into to track their work. But the opposite is true.
The system of record is the foundation agents run on
. It holds the context they read, the guardrails they work within, the tools they act through and the feedback that tells them whether it worked.
The models will keep changing. The record is the part that remembers.

Building software was already difficult when you had two types of users: builders who wanted complete flexibility and people who wanted simplicity. We call them dark and light users. Now there's a third: agents that need to read, reason and act across the same data, often without human intervention. And also a fourth dimension: your customer's customers, who interact directly with the agents built to serve them.

You cannot build the best product by picking a side. Collapse toward the dark builder and you've added complexity for a light user; collapse toward simplicity, and the builder leaves for something they can actually shape to their unique use case.

As agents become more autonomous, the value shifts from the interface where people work to the infrastructure that determines what agents know, what they're allowed to do and whether their actions can be trusted.
Agents aren't a feature bolted on, they're a new layer of users working internally and externally. We serve billions of API calls, millions of MCP tool actions and tens of thousands of custom agents.

Attio is moving from building tools for the team that serves customers to building agents that prospect, support and save accounts directly for them. Every one of those interactions is only as good as the record behind it.

We're figuring this out while our product and business expand to serve different types and sizes of companies, globally. That opens us up to even greater complexity, technical requirements, use cases, usage and, of course, expectations.
It blows my mind in the same way that trying to comprehend the size of the universe does.

blocks.text: Five problems worth building a career on
1. Engineering | Permissions and the write path

segments.t: How do you let thousands of agents act autonomously without compromising trust?

Human error has always existed in software. What's changing is the speed, scale and autonomy with which mistakes can propagate. An agent can write incorrect values across thousands of records before a human even knows something has gone wrong.

Permissions are a clear example of why it's really hard to build Attio. It has to be solved across every object, every surface, and every actor at once. Whether your team is ten humans or ten thousand agents, it's the same problem: nothing should act on context it shouldn't see. That's why row-level permissions are one of the biggest things on our roadmap. Then consider what holds it together when agents run unsupervised. What about conflict resolution when two agents and a person touch a record in the same second?

Solving these problems is changing how we build software in the first place. We're moving towards engineers spending less time writing and reviewing code and more time designing the architecture and guardrails, without lowering the craft required and quality bar.
Figuring all of this out is something our engineering team are running towards.

blocks.text: 2. Design | Distinction, now with a mystery user

segments.t: How do you make complex agent behaviour understandable without making the product complex?
Looking at a record, what a person said out loud on a call and what a model inferred from context needs distinction and an experience that builds trust.

Every record UI assumes a human made every edit, because until recently they did. Now it carries another meaning (who wrote this, how confident is it, has anyone checked), and that leads to different experiences: some invisible, others optimised for the human task, all constructed by the builder of the workflow. When an agent proposes 400 changes, what's the surface for approving them?

The goal isn't maximum autonomy. Each customer needs to choose how much autonomy to give at each step, and the design has to make that choice feel obvious. Some of these experiences won't have a screen at all.
There’s no dominant design pattern for making outcomes and progress feel inevitable, yet.
What should software cost when the amount of work no longer correlates with the number of people?

Per-seat pricing is a bet that humans are the unit of value. That bet doesn't hold on its own anymore. Do we need a platform fee for the shared context Attio provides? Should we keep seats for the humans? How many credits do you need for the work agents do?

Outcome pricing sounds better until you try to define an outcome across a whole world of use cases, business sizes and revenue models. Credits have to be flexible enough to keep processes running through a surge, with controls over who spends them and on what. And how do you price an agent that talks directly to your customer's customers?
Companies that get this right will define how software is monetised for the next decade.
How do you sell the value of a product that customers need to build with before they fully understand it?

For years, selling a CRM was a "why us" conversation. Everyone knew what a CRM was. Now it's a "why one" conversation for Attio, because we're explaining a category that didn't exist a year ago. Customers come to us knowing AI should change their go-to-market and we can show them how.

When a purchase decision is made, many others are supporting, watching and awaiting the decision. The buyer of a system of record is buying for the builders, the users and the agents. How do you demo what's possible without the prompts or the data in place? One of our reps answered that for a customer recently, demoing a fully populated instance, working web pages and a script timed to the minute. It advanced the buying decision by six months. Another example is our Solutions and Sales teams now building SDK apps live on calls with customers.
Your sales ability needs to be as flexible and technical as the product.
This is the one I live daily.
How do you hire exceptional people for problems nobody has solved before?

Our world is moving so fast that every role comes with some speculation, which makes calibration and commitment hard on both sides. But, quite wonderfully, it results in mission-driven, ambitious people who have great judgement.

Screening the profile doesn't add enough signal. But having great conversations is how you set the bar. The strongest signal I find, repeatedly, is people who have built systems. Often from a place of frustration that things should just be better. This drive helps me predict someone's performance in ambiguous territory better than brand signals or credentials.
I look for three things beyond the skills required for the role.
Drive: people who create change rather than wait to be asked.
Judgement: people who can make good decisions with incomplete information.
Systems thinking: people who improve the way work happens, rather than just complete tasks.

The flip side is the opportunity. Very few people will get the chance to solve problems like these from the inside, at the moment they're emerging. The people who do won't just build valuable skills. They'll learn to become force multipliers; people capable of transforming how entire organisations operate. And I believe they'll be the ones leading the next generation of companies.
It's the combination of drive, judgement and skill that makes people invaluable when the problems haven't been solved before.

The next generation of great software companies won't just provide tools for people to do their work. They'll provide the context, permissions and infrastructure for humans and agents to work together.

The Engineering, GTM, Marketing, Operations and Product challenges this creates are largely unsolved. That's what makes this such an extraordinary time to build at Attio. We're not just hiring people to scale what already works. We're hiring people to figure out what comes next.

title: Introducing the architecture for agentic revenue.
description: Agents are breaking software that was never intended for them. We're building the architecture for what comes next.
h1: Introducing the architecture for Agentic Revenue
toc: This is the architecture for agentic revenue.
The next phase for hybrid architecture.
excerpt: Agents are breaking software. We're building the architecture for what comes next.

segments.t: Agents can do the high context work of a person at the speed of a machine.
They unlock a radically personalized customer experiences at unprecedented scale.
But software wasn't built for agents.
So today, Attio is introducing a new shape of software.
It is
the first hybrid architecture engineered for people and agents in equal measure.
We’re launching four new capabilities: SQL Engine, Data Connectors, Agent Scale, and Activities, in beta. Together, they build on Attio’s core platform and make the
architecture for agentic revenue
, giving frontier teams the power to scale any revenue motion.

blocks.text: This is the architecture for agentic revenue.

segments.t: Attio combines the speed and scale of infrastructure with the context and control of application software, in one architecture built for people and agents.

It works at the speed of an agent, across your entire market, to the standard of your best rep. Every task an agent completes adds context for the next, so that context compounds with every interaction.
Three interconnected layers make it possible:
Context.
Every customer signal is captured in a shared context layer that stays current and grows richer with each interaction.
Orchestration.
Agents and workflows use this context to act on every signal across your revenue operations.
Ecosystem.
Connect Attio to all the tools and agents that run your business, with consistent access to its data, logic, and actions.
Every product we've shipped has laid the groundwork for this. Today, we're introducing four major advances that extend what it can do.

blocks.text: The next phase for hybrid architecture.

segments.t: Attio now speaks SQL, the data language of agents.

Agents use it to query millions of records and relationships at once and perform complex calculations directly in Attio. Questions that previously required exported datasets or custom reports can now be answered in a single query.
For example:
Find which lead sources produce the highest win rates on deals over $50,000.
Calculate weighted pipeline across regions and owners.
Identify open opportunities associated with churned customers.
Attio performs the calculation and returns an exact result. Every query is available to inspect

SQL also works inside Workflows, allowing the results to trigger actions. Identify accounts that cross a usage threshold and automatically create expansion opportunities, or calculate values across related records to route deals.
Attio now exposes a live, Postgres-compatible endpoint, connecting your CRM directly to your agents and data stack.

Connect Hex, Omni, Looker, Metabase, dbt, and other compatible tools using PostgreSQL credentials. Queries run directly against Attio, so dashboards and analytical tools can work with live CRM data without exports or synchronized copies.
Build weighted pipeline forecasts in your BI tool.
Track performance against custom targets.
Analyze deals across segments, teams, and regions.
When an opportunity changes, the updated data is immediately available to your connected tools.
Connections are read-only, with dedicated credentials that workspace admins can disable or regenerate.
For teams with an existing data stack, Attio becomes a live, directly queryable source. For teams building one, advanced analytics no longer requires a complex integration project.
A person might review a few dozen accounts in a day. An agent can work across thousands simultaneously.
Attio is engineered to support hundreds of millions of records.
Research every account in your market.
Continuously requalify your entire pipeline.
Keep millions of records current as new information becomes available.
Thousands of agents can work across your customer data, with the same permissions and access controls that govern the rest of Attio.
As your business grows, agents can take on more work without sacrificing the reliability your team depends on.
Not every important customer interaction happens in an email or meeting.
Activities extends Attio's data model to capture the most unique interactions as structured, first-class data, like support conversations, social DMs, product events, and more.
Define custom schemas for the activities that matter to your business.
Support escalation gets tags before a renewal conversation takes place.
Track expansion opportunities with detailed product events.
Give your team a more complete understanding of every relationship, and your agents the context they need to act on it.
SQL-powered questions in Ask Attio are available on all plans. Open Ask Attio and ask a question about your pipeline, performance, or customer data to get started.
SQL access through the REST API, MCP, and Workflows is available on Enterprise plans. Data Connectors are also available on Enterprise, and can be created and managed by workspace admins under
Workspace settings → Data → Data connectors
Activities is currently in beta.

title: Inside the system that runs Attio’s GTM
description: Kyle Doherty, Rev Ops Lead, and Zev Lebowitz, Head of Solutions, take you behind the scenes of how we centralize leads, customer interactions, and communication in Attio , and the wider tech stack that feeds into it.
h1: Inside the system that runs Attio’s GTM
toc: How a lead becomes an Attio customer
Watch how Attio uses Attio live
excerpt: Kyle Doherty, Rev Ops Lead, and Zev Lebowitz, Head of Solutions, take you behind the scenes of how we centralize leads, customer interactions, and communication in Attio, and the wider tech stack that feeds into it.

segments.t: Every customer interaction creates context. Most companies just don’t have it all in one place.

Product usage, sales conversations, support tickets, emails, and intent signals are spread across different systems, even though they all describe the same customer. Bringing them together gives every team a continuously improving picture of each relationship – and better information to act on.
Attio runs on Attio.

Every deal our Sales team works and every support conversation we have lives in the same CRM used by 35,000 other companies to run and scale their GTM. Product signups, inbound leads, support tickets, usage data, and more all feed into one shared context layer – so our team always knows where a relationship stands, without jumping between systems.
In this first edition of
How Attio uses Attio

, Kyle Doherty, Rev Ops Lead, and Zev Lebowitz, Head of Solutions, take you behind the scenes of how we centralize leads, customer interactions, and communication in Attio , and the wider tech stack that feeds into it.
Attio is the CRM for agentic revenue. We’re a Series B B2B SaaS company, with close to 200 people in the team.

We’re product-led, and we sell our product to a varied customer base: the fastest growing startups in the world, VCs, agencies, two-sided marketplaces, and traditional B2B businesses. Behind this motion sits our
GTM teams

: Account Executives (AE) and Solutions Engineers on the sales side, an onboarding function to drive early adoption, a Customer Success team that runs in two tiers, and a partnerships function of third-party consultants who provide broader go-to-market expertise around customers’ Attio deployment.
If you're a similar size, stage, or running a similar motion, most of what follows should map onto your setup.

blocks.text: How a lead becomes an Attio customer

segments.t: Every prospect has a different buying journey, and our GTM strategy is built around that. We let customers move through Attio on their own terms, while using fit, intent, and engagement signals to understand where team involvement can add the most value. That means Sales and Success can focus their time on the customers who need – or will benefit from – more hands-on support, without adding friction for everyone else.
Leads can enter through multiple channels, generate different signals, and engage with us in different ways. We bring that context together to decide how and when to engage.
Before we get into the tech stack, here’s how a lead becomes a customer at Attio.
Inbound leads reach our funnel through various of channels. Most begin by signing up for Attio and starting a
free trial
, while others arrive through our Talk to Sales form, applications to our
Startup Program
, the chat on our marketing site, and enquiries to consultants from our
Experts directory

We run outbound too, and we treat it as signal-driven rather than purely list-based. Outbound leads are segmented on three main things: their relationship to us (known or net new), their fit score, and their intent and engagement signals.

All of these factors paint a picture of how close a team is to buying, and determine how we engage with them. If a lead has interacted with us before, the messaging and engagement shift to reflect that. Every lead is enriched, segmented, and scored, and their fit score decides whether they become self-serve or sales-assist. Signals tell us where they are in their buying journey, which sets what we send and how they get prioritized.

Anyone can self-service on their own to become a customer, and prospects do not have to speak to a member of our Sales team to buy the product. Customers vary in ICP fit and value, so we invest human effort in the fastest-growing and highest-value prospects. Letting everyone else self-serve frees our Sales team to reach out proactively to those prospects, with a reason for them to engage. This set up raises close rates and makes every touchpoint with a customer worth having.

Leads with strong intent and fit to our ICP flow to our Sales team for review and routing, with the potential for them to reach out and start a human-owned sales cycle. It makes sure that high-priority customers get personalised support and advice during their buying journey, and that everyone gets a first-class experience however they enter the funnel.

We have a variety of onboarding offerings, ranging from one-on-one enablement with our Solutions team, to one-to-many group workshops, to self-service content. Every new paying customer is automatically reviewed and assigned an appropriate amount of onboarding support based on their contract, firmographics, and growth signals, regardless of whether they’ve engaged with our Sales team.

We have scaled one-to-many program for the broader customer base, and one-to-one support for individual accounts. The same process we run at onboarding is mirrored here, where every account is reviewed regardless of previous engagement. The team works from renewal timing, churn alerts, and adoption context to spot where to step in, identifying upsells, conversions, and accounts that need additional support.
Here’s how our Attio workspace is configured, and what each
object
lets us track.

Everyone at Attio syncs their email into Attio, which creates and maintains our Company and Person records. Our inbound lead channels also create and enrich company and people records, which are automatically enriched, and aid in lead triage and prioritization.
We run Leads and Deals on a single Deal object. It gives us one object to maintain instead of several across the pipeline, and our Sales team gets one continuous record of a customer’s journey.

Using the Deals object pays off in segmenting and reporting too, as it removes the friction of working with other objects and relationships. Slice the Deal object by type, stage, and more, and you have the segment you want to action or analyze.

Workspaces represent every existing customer, those in a trial or paying. A Workspace record mirrors what’s happening in the product itself, so we have live, always-enriched data on every customer’s activity.
Intercom tickets:
Every support ticket is synced into Attio as a custom object, so support interactions live alongside Attio data.
Onboarding Records:

The customer onboarding process also runs on a custom object, to track the progress and health of each new customer as they adopt Attio. It ensures each customer gets the attention they need, and that no customers fall through the cracks during the first critical weeks and months of their lifecycle as a customer.
Experts:

Our team uses Attio to manage the pipeline of new and existing experts, who play a key role in our customer's adoption of the product. Sales and Partnerships teams also see incoming requests for Expert help in one place, and linking those requests to deals provides a clearer view of how the program moves win rates, adoption, and retention.
Applications:
Attio’s
applications and integrations

are also tracked on a custom object. It holds every third-party app in our ecosystem, including its category, install count, and the date it shipped. Understanding what apps a customer has installed gives our team context on their broader GTM stack and motion.
These apps are built with Attio's
App SDK
, which lets people extend Attio with their own interface, server logic, and workflow automation. Apps run on Attio's infrastructure and appear inside the product itself.

Attio acts as the central layer across our GTM stack. Data from the tools we use across marketing, sales, product, and support flows into the CRM, creating a consolidated view of every customer and opportunity. That shared context helps our teams surface stronger signals, prioritize the right accounts, and make more informed decisions.

Segment is our instrumentation and distribution layer for in-product data. It’s a customer data platform (CDP) that captures all events from Attio, allowing our Sales team to see what customers are actually doing in-product alongside context provided by Attio.

Segment feeds new Workspace signup events and usage signals into Attio in real-time, which allows our team to triage inbound leads quickly and spot expansion signals, such as a Workspace hitting a seat threshold, or a key feature being activated for the first time.

Subscription and payment data originate in Attio, with Stripe as the processor. Self-serve customers on trial and paid plans are billed through Stripe directly, as do customers who convert from trial to paid or change billing methods. Subscription details, like purchased product and current subscription, are synced from our application to Attio through Segment.
Our core product data is the starting point for all things GTM - it gives us the live story behind every customer, powering insights like health scoring, PLG triggers, and Customer Success workflows.
Beyond product signups, we have several other inbound lead channels which flow directly into Attio:
Talk to Sales
form fills and applications for our
Startup Program
Forms on our site that feed our deal triage workflows.
Fin for Sales:

In addition to powering our in-app Support chat, Fin chat acts as an SDR on our marketing website. When prospects interact with the chat on the marketing website, Fin qualifies them and creates Deal records in Attio for our Sales team to pick up.
Partnerpage:
Our directory of
Attio Experts
, who are certified Attio consulting partners. When a customer reaches out to an Expert on the directory, it’s logged to create a Deal or update an existing account team.

Clay handles enrichment and signal detection, and Claude Code is used to run custom prospecting workflows. Every Company record runs through a segmenting and triage workflow, which decides whether it needs to go to Clay for enrichment. These records land in Clay tables, and the attributes Clay enriches are written back to the corresponding Company record in Attio.

Lemlist is used as the primary outbound sequencing tool, running multi-channel campaigns that feed activity data back into Attio. Activity events, such as sends, replies, clicks, and LinkedIn touches, all flow back into Attio for full visibility alongside the prospect’s deal and email history. This allows the team to see outbound engagement in full context with the rest of the prospect’s record.
Once a meeting is booked, an outbound deal record is created.
We use Fin for Support interactions, which are synced into Attio as a custom object and live alongside Attio data.

While Segment handles acquisition and top-of-funnel signals, more granular platform data, such as feature adoption, workflow usage, and session activity all live in BigQuery, our data warehouse. We build aggregated health and usage metrics in BigQuery and use Polytomic to sync them into Attio as Workspace or User attributes. These signals power things like PQLs, churn alerts, renewal signals, and upsell context.
Polytomic also syncs Attio record data back to BigQuery, where it provides critical customer context to our marketing, product usage, and finance data sets.

We use Customer.io for customer marketing and lifecycle marketing. As part of our Success motion, data is synced to Customer.io directly from Segment and Attio, and we use Attio to catch signals that drive scaled programs like product adoption, referrals, and annual renewals, as well as targeted campaigns. This means that all campaign enrolment in Customer.io is driven by true activity tracking, based on the prospect or customer’s stage in their journey with Attio.

title: What AI can't change: Behind Attio's latest brand campaign
description: AI is changing how sales gets done, research, follow-up, pipeline. Here's why Attio built a campaign around the one thing that doesn't change: the celebration.
h1: What AI can’t change: Behind Attio’s latest brand campaign
toc: The work changes. The celebration doesn’t.
For teams already living the shift
excerpt: Why Attio's latest brand campaign is built around the one part of sales AI doesn't touch: the celebration itself.

segments.t: Sales is changing quickly.

AI is reshaping how revenue teams research accounts, prospect, qualify leads, follow up, manage pipeline and decide what to do next. Work that once depended on people manually moving information between systems can increasingly be understood and acted on by the platform itself.
Attio is built for that shift. As the Agentic CRM, Attio gives teams a system that understands the context around customers and prospects, surfaces what matters and can increasingly act on it.
For our latest brand campaign, we wanted to bring that vision to a much bigger audience.
But rather than build a campaign around everything AI is changing, we became interested in the inverse question:
If the way sales happens is changing this much, what stays the same?

blocks.text: The work changes. The celebration doesn’t.

segments.t: There is no shortage of advertising about the future of AI.

Revenue teams are surrounded by the same promises about obsolete workflows, outdated stacks and agents taking over more of the work. What felt novel even six months ago can quickly become part of the background.
We wanted to say something different about the shift.
We kept coming back to the feeling of winning, and to the team celebration that surrounds it.

The work leading up to a win can change dramatically. Platforms can research an account, keep itself up to date, identify the next action and increasingly take that action itself. But when a team finally lands a customer they have been chasing for months, hits a number they were not sure they would hit, or gets the yes they have been working towards for multiple quarters, the feeling is familiar.
Teams have rituals for those moments. A message in the sales channel. A high five. A fist bump. A handshake. A particular emoji. A dinner after a big quarter.
The rituals differ, but what they represent is the same: a shared moment when the work pays off.
AI is changing a huge amount of what happens before the win. We don’t think it changes what the win feels like.
That became the centre of the campaign.

blocks.text: For teams already living the shift

segments.t: The founders, revenue leaders and GTM teams we are speaking to do not need to be told that AI is changing sales. They are already leading that shift.
They are experimenting with new tools, rebuilding processes and reconsidering what should still require manual work. At the same time, the role of the CRM itself is changing.
The traditional CRM model relies on people continually feeding information into a database and maintaining it well enough to make that information useful. The next generation looks very different.
Attio is the platform that understands the context around customers and prospects, connects signals from across the business, and gives both people and agents the context they need to act.
That is a significant product story. The challenge was expressing the ambition behind it without trying to explain the entire product on a billboard.
Instead, we focused the campaign on what all of that technology is in service of: smarter work, more leverage for the team, and ultimately, better outcomes.
The route to those outcomes may change. The desire to win does not.

We did not start with celebrations. Early creative territory explored Attio as the platform behind the win: the system creating momentum, the advantage that compounds, the technology behind better outcomes.

Marketing and Studio developed the copy and visual together, working through more than 250 iterations before the words held up on their own. The breakthrough was simple: the campaign didn’t need to draw a line between “AI work” and “human work”. The work leading up to a win could change dramatically while the feeling at the end remained familiar.
Every team has its own rituals for marking a win, a high five, a fist bump, a handshake nobody outside the room would recognise.

Hands became the shorthand for that moment. By getting close to the gesture, the images could stay deliberately ambiguous. You do not know whether the people have just landed the biggest customer in company history or hit their quarter. You only know that something went right.
That ambiguity leaves room for something else to sit beside it: a claim about where sales is going. The image stays familiar. The claim looks forward. That tension is the campaign.
Sales will look very different in the months ahead.

Teams will spend less time maintaining systems and doing work that software can handle for them. Platforms will understand more of the context around every customer and prospect, and agents will take on a growing share of the work around every revenue motion.
That shift is already happening.
But the win itself will still matter. There will still be a customer the team wants to land, a number everyone cares about, and a moment when they realise they got there.
And there will still be a ritual that marks it.
That is the part we built the campaign around.
Sales is changing. This feeling isn’t.

title: Why Attio hires graduates
description: We look for what you've built, not where you studied. Discover why graduates thrive at Attio through our Graduate Startup Program.
excerpt: The bet on early talent that keeps paying off.

segments.t: Today we are opening up applications for our fourth cohort of Graduate Associates.
The program runs for six months, after which successful Graduates are offered a full-time role at Attio.

Attio’s Graduate Program is a core part of our talent philosophy. We have had three years of immense success hiring ambitious, high potential early career builders into the business, giving them an irresponsible amount of responsibility and seeing their careers flourish.

People who thrive at Attio are high energy, curious, first-principles problem solvers. Graduates have them all in abundance. There is no playbook for redefining a software category, and working from first principles is the way you continuously improve. Graduates come with unique questions and fresh perspectives where inexperience becomes a strength, and the curiosity early talent brings lifts the whole company.

Our Graduates have also been some of the strongest leaders in pushing forward new ways of working across the company, supercharged by AI. Everyone accepted into the program is a builder, regardless of background or degree - they all share a high agency attitude to building great outcomes for everyone around them.

“In my first three months I was trusted to create an inbound AI sales agent that would reach tens of thousands of website leads. Two months and thousands of conversations later, with six figures in attributed revenue, I was on stage doing a Q&A on how I built it, in front of hundreds of founders, revenue leaders and sales managers. Taking a project of that scale from idea to build in my first months is the kind of responsibility this program gives you. Attio is a great fit for anyone who turns "someone should build this" into something actually built.”
Will Jones
Graduate Associate (GTM), Class of 2026
We hire an intentionally small group of people so that each individual has a large surface area of opportunity. Nothing is off limits if you are capable of owning it.

Giving so much scope to early career talent only works with a strong support system. Every Graduate is paired with a Graduate Sponsor who is responsible for their career development, mentorship and providing direct feedback on their work. Graduates meet with their Sponsors daily in the first few weeks - it is delightfully intense with fast feedback.

Additionally all Graduates meet as a group weekly with a Graduate Advisor to give them wider context on the business and the tech ecosystem, what’s happening in the market, why we are making certain bets, what’s working and what’s not. The transparency is what gives each individual a front row seat into one of the fastest growing technology businesses in Europe.
We are hiring Graduates in three areas of the business:
Go-to-Market:
GTM Engineering, Customer Success & Support, Partnerships
Marketing:
Growth, Campaigns, Lifecycle
Operations:
Office of the CEO, Product Operations, General Operations
We do not screen for a specific degree, background or a polished CV. Instead we look for evidence of what applicants have built, achieved, and approaches to problems that haven’t been seen before.

The past three years of success have forged our next generation of Attio leaders. blocks.text: Functions that understand change over time

segments.t: Attribute history functions work with historical values, helping you understand how your data has changed over time, not just what it is now.
timeSpentIn
measures how long an attribute sat at a certain value, like a deal stage.
hasBeenIn
checks whether it ever passed through a given value.
valueAt
tells you what an attribute was on a specific date,
previousValue
checks what it was before the last change, and
valueSetAt
pinpoints when it changed.
These custom functions open up insights that are only possible in Attio.
Every computed value becomes context to inform your next move.

The formula output is an input to everything else in Attio. Filter and group views by it. Use it as a metric in reports and dashboards. Trigger a workflow when it crosses a specific threshold. Pull it into a sequence to personalize outreach.
You get live insights with logic that runs through every part of Attio.
Formulas strengthen the foundation of Attio in three ways.
Deterministic.

The same inputs give you the same answer, every time. That’s what makes a number safe to forecast on, audit in a board meeting, or trigger a workflow from. You don’t want a creative answer to "what’s this deal worth?". You want the right one.
Composable.

A formula can reference another formula and other attributes. Set your stage probabilities once, then use them in weighted pipeline, in a report, and in a scoring model. Formulas stack, so you can use them everywhere.
Reactive.

When the underlying data changes, the formula recalculates on its own, within seconds. If seat count changes, contract value follows. Nothing to re-run, nothing to re-prompt, nothing to remember. And none of this slows down as you grow.
Precise, connected, and current. That’s what makes a value in Attio better than a number anywhere else.

segments.t: As your go-to-market team grows, the role of your CRM expands across the organization. More roles rely on it, more data lives inside it, and more company decisions depend on it.
Companies need a way to ensure that the right teams can get the right access to the right data, without slowing anyone down.

That’s why today we're introducing a completely new permissions system in Attio, with object controls, team-based access, and an additive hierarchy. Together, you now have precise control over how access works across your entire workspace.

This isn't just additional settings. It's a foundational infrastructure layer designed to support the way growing teams actually work, with shared ownership, cross-functional visibility, and data everyone can trust.
You can now adjust the access level for every object in your workspace, with options for Read only, Read and write, and Full access.
Read only
: Can view all record data for the object, but cannot update it.
Read and write
: Can view and update record data for the object.
Full access
: Can manage object settings including permissions and attributes, and can view and update record data for the object.

This means your sales team can own the Deals object while giving others read-only visibility. Or an exec can manage specific object settings, like creating and managing attributes, without needing admin access to the full workspace.
Instead of managing permissions one person at a time, you can now create teams and grant access to entire groups at once.
Create a Sales team, a CS team, a Finance team, an Ops team, etc. Then reuse those groups across objects, lists, dashboards, workflows, and sequences.
When someone joins or changes roles, you update their team membership once and access flows everywhere it needs to.
Setting access permissions follows a clear hierarchy: workspace, then team, then individual member, where the most permissive grant always wins.
Start with safe defaults at the workspace level, then grant more access to specific teams or people when necessary.
Want to protect deal data while still sharing visibility? Set workspace access to “Read only” on the Deals object, then grant “Read and write” access to the Sales team and “Full access” to RevOps.
The best CRMs don't just store data. They give teams the confidence to put more data in, and the structure to collaborate around it safely.
That's the shift this launch enables. With the right controls in place, teams are more willing to centralize their work in the CRM. More data flows in. Cross-team visibility increases.

title: How we chose the name Attio | Attio
description: Your brand name, and by extension your domain, is the heartbeat of your company. Here's the story behind how we chose the name Attio.
h1: How we chose the name Attio
excerpt: Your brand name, and by extension your domain, is the heartbeat of your company. Here's the story behind how we chose the name Attio.

segments.t: Choosing a name is no small feat. It’s the heartbeat of your company, the first impression you make on potential customers, and the foundation of your brand identity. With over 362 million domain registrations across all TLDs, finding something unique, memorable, and available is even harder.

When preparing to launch Attio, we went on a journey to find the right name and make sure the domain would be available. From navigating high domain prices, compounding words, inventing new ones, and ultimately trusting our instincts - it was a process that challenged us at every turn. But in the end, we found a name that felt right for who we were and who we wanted to become. Here’s the story behind how we chose the name Attio.

Securing the right domain is one of the toughest challenges when launching a startup. Your domain is the epicenter of your brand - where potential customers go to learn about what you do, where you convert most of your customers and, in our case, where users access our product every day.

When we were choosing our name, we were aware that several TLDs like .co and .io were fashionable amongst startups - largely because they tend to be more readily available. Despite that trend, having a .com domain was our one non-negotiable requirement. As Paul Graham puts it:

"The problem with not having the .com of your name is that it signals weakness. Unless you're so big that your reputation precedes you, a marginal domain suggests you're a marginal company." - Paul Graham
It's the gold standard for any brand. So we knew we needed a .com domain.
We initially took a targeted approach: we created a shortlist of potential names - mostly interesting one-word domains like
flow.com
- and began researching availability, tracking down the owners, and submitting offers.

Unsurprisingly, one-word .com domains don’t come cheap. Seven-figure openers weren't uncommon, with the lowest priced domains starting in the low six-figures. Although the response rate was promising, we quickly realized that this approach wasn’t viable for us - we had only raised a pre-seed round at this point.
We needed a new strategy.
Despite there being ~170,000 words in the English language, a fair proportion of these won't make a brand name and the rest are almost certainly already parked by professional domain resellers.
So, we turned to compound words.
This opened up a wealth of possibilities, but an infinite number of combinations to research is a lot. To help narrow down our options, we created two lists:
Primary words:
These were words related to our product’s goals, our company’s mission, and were short (one or two syllables) for ease of compounding.
Secondary words:
These were words that worked well as endings and were relatively neutral.
One spreadsheet later and we had this:
We began scanning through hundreds of possible combinations, and we categorized our options into three groups:
Black
: Good, but currently taken.
Blue:
Good, taken, but potentially purchasable.
Green:
Good and available.

Even though there are many successful companies with compound names (think Dropbox, Facebook, YouTube, or PayPal), nothing felt quite right. Not to mention the fact that searching through hundreds of sub-par names for a rough diamond is a painstaking process - we decided to change tack again.
If one-word domains were too expensive and compound names were too limiting, what about inventing a new word?
We found an incredibly useful tool:
instantdomainsearch.com
We began experimenting with different combinations of letters to find something that was available but also reflected the brand identity we wanted to build.

blocks.label: domain name search   instant domain search 5 february 2025 2 3

segments.t: Of course, we couldn’t just mash the keyboard and hope for the best. There's a general pattern that English words follow in order to make sense.
Only certain letters can be repeated twice in a row (
t
p
r
d
b
l
and
s
No letter can be repeated three times in a row.
Vowels and consonants rarely group in sets greater than two.
After several sprints, we had come up with the following shortlist of potential names:
neve.com
rifio.com
simira.com
mirona.com
osiras.com
tallio.com
arias.com
And of course,
attio.com

If the process sounds a little random, it's because it was. But over time, we found ourselves getting into the rhythm of it and making some real progress. Names like Twilio, Vercel, and Monzo were reminders that creating a new word is entirely possible, and sometimes it leads to something great.
Once we had our shortlist, we had to pick our favorite. To make the final decision, we had to weigh four key factors:
Spelling
: If someone heard the name, would they know how to spell it? Could they easily type it into Google a few hours later?
Pronunciation

: Would it work in different accents? Would someone immediately understand you, or would you be left forever repeating it to potential customers? If people only ever read it, would pronunciation be uniform?
Competitiveness
: Could we rank at the top of search results? Could we secure matching social media handles to ensure consistency across platforms? Were trademarks available to protect our name?
Feel
: We all experience a myriad of brand names on a daily basis. As a result, almost everyone has a great sense for when a brand name
feels right
. We didn’t want our name to have any negative associations, and we wanted it to have the ability to be
big.
No prizes for guessing which one we settled on.

Ultimately, a brand name is what you make of it. How your tone of voice, product quality, and visual identity are perceived fill a name with personality and meaning. Apple was once just a fruit. Google was a misspelling. Attio was just a made-up word - until we made it ours. It’s the people behind the name and our team's dedication to incredible work that bring the name Attio to life.

title: A new vision for CRM | Attio
description: We're going to usher CRM into the AI era, and it will represent a monumental shift for the category. Here's our vision for the next generation of CRM.
h1: AI and the next generation of CRM
excerpt: We're going to usher CRM into the AI era, and it will represent a monumental shift for the category. Here's our vision for the next generation of CRM.

segments.t: Since the release of GPT-3 in June 2020, Large Language Models (LLMs) have expanded and evolved at an impressive rate. As their capabilities have grown, they’ve captured our imaginations with their novel abilities and ease of access.

It is now clear that AI represents the most significant shift in the technology landscape since the inception of the internet. And CRM, a $58 billion category and the engine of businesses everywhere, is now having a do-or-die moment. Simply adding LLM features to legacy architectures isn’t enough.

This moment echoes a similar shift back in 1999, when Salesforce took CRM into the internet era, building it from the ground up for the cloud. Today, the category is facing another paradigm shift, but the stakes are even higher.
Now, with AI, CRM is finally about to undergo a massive transformation. At Attio, we've been building for the next era of CRM since day one.
We're going to usher CRM into the AI era, and it will represent a monumental shift for the category. Today, we'll share our vision for the next generation of CRM.
The implications of AI for CRM are obviously profound. To understand why, we need to take a step back and look at the technology that's making this all possible: Large Language Models.

LLMs represent a monumental shift for software. They’re the foundation of modern AI, letting machines understand and generate human language in ways never before possible. They have two key capabilities:
Converting unstructured data into structured data

. LLMs can take all the unstructured data we generate (like emails, messages, videos and phone calls) and turn it into structured data that’s easy to work with, like categories, summaries or action items. In other words, they can take the way humans naturally communicate and make it useful for automation, insights, and reporting.
Reversing structured data into unstructured output.

Conversely, LLMs can also take structured data and turn it into natural language. They can use structured data to respond to questions, summarize complex data, records or even draft emails and messages.

Early attempts to integrate AI so far have largely focused on that second part: taking structured data and turning it into natural language. We’ve seen a lot of chatbots, copilots, and short injections of AI, like providing assistance in drafting or summarizing information. These features are useful and are already bringing meaningful productivity increases, but they’re the first step in bigger things to come.

The next big impact from AI will come from being able to convert unstructured data to structured data. For CRM, this means a platform where LLMs are natively embedded into the CRM’s core architecture and functionality, instead of being bolted on. This will create two seismic shifts for the category:
First, CRMs will gain the ability to understand and process vast amounts of unstructured data, in ways that were previously thought to be impossible.

Think about all the valuable information that's locked away in emails, video calls, phone calls and messages. Right now, this unstructured data is reluctantly and sporadically entered by humans, in bits and pieces. But with the right, AI-native data model in place, all of those insights can be automatically captured, structured, and put to work.

However, context won’t just be gleaned from language (e.g., call transcripts). Multi-modal AI models will process audio and video to understand not just words, but also tone, emotions, and the nuances of human interactions. If a client sounds excited or frustrated during a call, the AI will pick up on that. This deeper understanding will give your CRM human-like context for decision-making, as if you had your best teammate by your side for every interaction, catching all the subtle cues and providing valuable insights.

Second, your CRM will gain “agency.” Agency is the ability of an LLM to use complex reasoning capabilities to autonomously work towards a goal by breaking it down into smaller steps, deciding what actions to take at each step, and then using a set of predefined tools to execute those actions.

You’ll have multiple agents that perform complex tasks and workflows on your behalf, making intelligent choices along the way. Working together, they’ll be able to automate even the most complex business processes, including ones that require human judgment and nuance.

These two capabilities, when combined, will lead to a real paradigm shift for CRM. Go-to-market processes that used to require build-outs and complex configurations will become much simpler to implement. Tasks that previously required significant manual effort or complex automation will now be handled autonomously and intelligently by the CRM itself, but always under your direction and control. You set the goals and parameters, and the CRM executes with unprecedented efficiency and intelligence.

For years now, CRM has been on the cusp of revolution. The traditional paradigm reached its limits a long time ago. It was never designed to handle the exponential growth of data we've seen in the past decades.

At Attio, we recognized this impending shift. Since day one, we've been deliberately building for a paradigm change, intentionally designing a powerful, flexible product with strong fundamentals, ready for the next evolution of CRM.
With this foundation in place, Attio is now going to usher CRM into the AI era, and it will represent a monumental shift for the category.

Attio will be able to completely understand structured and unstructured data and act on it, eliminating day-to-day manual data entry, automating human tasks that were previously thought impossible to automate, and becoming an intelligent partner in every aspect of going to market.
Here’s how we’re doing it:

Building CRM for the AI era requires more than just incorporating LLMs into existing systems. It demands a fundamental reimagining of the CRM data model – one built from the ground up to work natively with AI.
This is where
Attio Objects

comes in. We built this powerful data model to be the modern system of record for businesses. It has custom objects, so it can match any business or data model, and it can handle massive workloads with millions of records with 50 milliseconds or less of latency.

But what really sets Attio Objects apart is how its fundamental design lends itself so well to AI models. We built it to be flexible and structured, with precise data types, rather than treating everything as simple strings. Each property in our data model holds semantic context about the information it represents.

This approach, which was crucial for us in creating a powerful system of record, is also incredibly important for AI integration. When an LLM interacts with Attio, it's not just seeing a collection of data – it's interfacing with a structured representation of your business.

When describing your data structure to an LLM, Attio Objects doesn't present just a random collection of information. Instead, it offers a rich semantic graph of your business. This allows the AI to truly understand the context of each piece of information. For instance, the LLM can distinguish that a particular field represents a currency value in USD, or recognize the difference between an email address and a phone number.

Fundamentally, Attio’s data model doesn’t just give a powerful way of storing information, but also a sophisticated method of representing it. This representation is invaluable to LLMs when they're reasoning, summarizing, or automating tasks, as they can understand that a specific field has a particular meaning and adjust its operations accordingly.

The CRM should be the all-knowing, central source of truth for your business. But the reality is that no matter how many integrations you have, it still needs context to function (which is almost always manual). Think how many sales reps have data entry stipulated in their performance goals, or even in their contracts. And without that data, your business can’t move.
In the near future, Attio will automatically ingest and understand
all
of your data – both structured, like we do now, and
unstructured

data – the details and aspects of every video call, meeting, email, document, or even data from the web. As mentioned earlier, this goes beyond language. Your CRM will know not just the meaning of words being spoken, but also the tone and body language of the customer.

Your CRM will autonomously and consistently extract insights, populate attributes, and trigger workflows based on the content of emails, video calls, and other customer interactions. As a result, Attio will be able to understand and process data in ways that were previously thought impossible.

For example, imagine a feature that can automatically derive the value of a deal based on what was said during a sales call. By ingesting the unstructured data of the call in real time, understanding the context, and cross-referencing with external data sources and your CRM data, Attio could intelligently infer the deal size – without the sales rep ever having to manually enter that information in an attribute.
For the first time, manual data entry will no longer be a barrier to having a complete, up-to-date view of your customer relationships.
Once you have complete context, you can then use Attio’s intelligent agents to drive every GTM process, even ones that were thought to be impossible to automate because they require human judgment.

Attio will be the place where you architect your entire GTM strategy. Our vision is that built-in AI agents will help you run your business so you can focus on high-value, high-impact work. They will take the manual work out of your daily business workflows and processes, even if they involve human judgment or input.

Early attempts at standalone agents for businesses are already available, offering anthropomorphic helpers like “Tom” and “Eva,” ready to assist you with your business. While these may prove to be useful tools, their long-term potential is capped by their specificity and the shape of their product.

We believe that the future of AI in CRM does not mean having an army of virtual assistants at your disposal. These standalone helpers, while novel, are ultimately limited by their separation from your core business data and processes.

In Attio, intelligent agents will not be personified, and they will be intricately woven into the platform. They’ll automate even the most complex tasks and processes, and continuously learn and improve.

They’ll be seamlessly incorporated into the CRM, working in the background to help your business run. These will come by default in the product, configurable under the hood, and with the ability to create as many as you want. You’ll have fine-grained control over how they operate.

The goal is to make you more productive and powerful, but in a way that feels natural and effortless. You won't be constantly reminded that you're interacting with AI – you'll simply find yourself accomplishing more, with less effort.

Attio’s AI capabilities will extend beyond action and data ingestion: they’ll be embedded into nearly every interaction a user has with the platform. This will create a completely new type of user experience.

Attio will provide intelligent suggestions and even guidance based on your interactions as you work. When you’re on a call with a prospect, Attio will take notes, pick up on verbal cues, and then suggest a specific case study to mention based on something your prospect just said.

Our platform will be an intelligent partner at every step, making dynamic, context-based decisions based on the real-time ingestion of all your data, and even adjusting the interface based on how you work. It will continuously learn and improve over time, adapting to your unique business needs and processes.
You’ll also be able to interact with Attio using natural language commands and questions for virtually every aspect of running your business, from building sales pipelines to creating new workflows.

The goal is to make you more productive and powerful, but in a way that feels natural and effortless. You won't be constantly reminded that you're interacting with AI – you'll simply find yourself accomplishing more, with less effort.
This is the future of CRM user experience – an evolution that amplifies your capabilities while fading into the background. It's AI that empowers you, without overshadowing you.
The arrival of LLMs has sparked a lot of discussion about how CRM will evolve. The most common refrain is that CRM is going to go from being a system of record to a system of action.
But this isn’t quite right. To take action, you need context. And to have context, you need data. The truth is that the next generation of CRM will need to be all three of these things.

At Attio, we're building a CRM that doesn't just ingest data and act, but also understands, learns and adapts. It's a closed-loop system where every action will feed back into the system, informing future decisions and constantly refining its understanding of your business.
Just as Salesforce ushered in the CRM for the cloud era, Attio will do so for the AI era.
For the first time ever, CRM will finally be able to deliver on its promise to not just deeply understand your entire business, but to actively help you run it – and get better at doing so over time.

segments.t: In product-led growth, the metrics are the signals. Who's activating, who's expanding, who's about to leave , every move a customer makes shows up in the data before it shows up in revenue.

The trick is catching those signals when they happen, and turning them into action while the moment's still warm. Below are three PLG metrics worth monitoring, and the workflow you'd build in Attio to act on each one.
Before you start

What follows are three of the most useful metrics to watch in a PLG motion, each paired with a workflow that turns the metric's movement into action.

Activation rate is the share of new signups who hit a meaningful first-value milestone in a defined window: completing onboarding, sending the first invite, running the first job, whatever your product calls "the moment it clicks." It's the most important top-of-funnel signal in PLG. Healthy activation means the rest of the funnel has fuel; a leaky activation rate means everything else suffers.
The workflow that acts on this signal watches new signups for whether they reach activation, and surfaces the ones who don't to a CSM with a brief on what they've done so far.

blocks.label: Try this in Ask Attio
blocks.text: For every new signup, track whether they reach our activation milestones within 7 days. If they don't, send a Slack notification to the CS team channel with the user's name, account, and last activity date.

segments.t: Engagement is the running pulse of an active account: how often users log in, how many features they touch, how deep they go. In PLG, engagement is the leading indicator of both expansion (climbing engagement means a team finding new use cases) and churn (declining engagement means a team drifting away). The number you watch matters less than the trend over time.
The workflow that acts on this signal watches engagement week-over-week and flags accounts whose trend has shifted, so a CSM or AM can act before the move shows up in retention numbers.

blocks.label: Try this in Ask Attio
blocks.text: Every Monday morning, find paying customer accounts that haven't had any product activity in the past 14 days. Post the list to the CS team Slack channel with their MRR and assigned CSM.

segments.t: NRR measures how much revenue your existing customers represent at the end of a period compared to the start, including expansion, contraction, and churn. In PLG, NRR is the single best indicator of motion velocity: a number above 100% means existing customers grew enough to cover any you lost; below 100% means leaks somewhere. Leadership reads it monthly; the board reads it quarterly.
The workflow that acts on this signal monitors the components of NRR across cohorts and surfaces the accounts driving the biggest moves, up or down.

blocks.label: Try this in Ask Attio
blocks.text: When a paying customer's MRR drops by more than 20% in a single billing cycle, send a Slack message to the AM channel with the account name, old MRR, new MRR, and the assigned AM.
